sentences.text: This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 2.

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 5/21 (416), 6/14 (412), 7/15 (209), 24 (203), 25 (416), 8/1/1 (015),  (016),
2(416), 11 (416), 12/1 (112), LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 9/1 (412), 18/1 (406), 10 (410), 19/5/2 (209), 25/1/2 (204), 2/1 (206), 9/2 (111), 10/1 (212), 4/14 (501), 17 (510) i.e. total area measuring 66 Bigha and 12 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (in short, the said land).

5. It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6.

Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :

sentences.text: i) The LAC has not considered that the said land is very fertile and fit for all commercial, residential, industrial, etc purposes and the said land is levelled more than 2 feet height from the nearby land.
The said land bears no defects but the LAC has assessed the market value at very low rate.
ii) The revenue estate of Village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Delhi Rohtak Road (Nangloi).

The said estate is surrounded by many prestigious colonies/village/ Industries area, etc and the value of each every commodity has been raised day by day, the value of which has also been increased day by day.
LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 iii)

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said Land has got potential value as many purposes and the same has been surrounded by Villages Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, Kirari, Nithari, etc and it the market value is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and hence has a great market value.

The land enjoys all type of modern facilities/ amenities like developed telephone,
electricity, water connection, public school, Govt. School and most frequently severed by DTC,
Railway Station and other transportation.

v) The LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the land rather he has wholly and solely relied on the policy announcement and which come into effect from the financial year 20012002 in which the Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land at the rate of Rs. 15.70 lacs per acre for the acquisition of the Agricultural land.
The LAC has further not made any efforts to find out the market value of the land in the village.

vi) The land of the petitioners is surrounded by DDA PhaseII, DSIDC Project Bawana, PVC market Tikri Kalan, Indene bottling Plant Ghevra, Nangloi, Mundka Railway Station, Metro Project Mundka, National Highway No. 10, Village Pooth Kalan, Budh Vihar, Rama Vihar, Rithala, Karala just near the famous colonies Prem Nagar, Agar Nagar, Rani Khera and Colony, Madanpur Dabas,
Sir Chhotu Ram Institute of Engineering, Ganga International School, Maharaja Agarsen Institute of LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs.
Union of India Page no. 5 of 11

Management and market value in the above said area are not less than Rs. 5,000/
per sq. yards.

vii) The petitioner's land is situated just near 100 mtr. Road which is connected to Sector 30, 31,
32, 21, 22, 28 and 29 (connected National Highway No. 1 to 10) and Chhotu Ram Institute of Technology, Netaji Subhash Tourist Complex, and famous prestigious school Ganga International Maharaja Agarsen Institution are a stone throw from the land of the claimant.

Land of the claimant is quite adjacent to the Abadi area of Village Mundka, Ghevra, and Kirari Suleman Nagar, nangloi and there are thousands of industries working in the above said surrounding area, thus, the market Jai Bhagwan Ors.

7. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 5,000/ per sq.
yards.
The petitioners have claimed a solatium @ 30% on the market value and additional amount.
Interest at the amount due to the petitioners in accordance with the law and all other statutory benefits with damages of the crops @ Rs. 1,00,000/ per acre.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/ Land Acquisition Collector (North West) and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the reference petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in erspect of the relief claimed.

The LAC has correctly LAC no. 67/
2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors.

Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 assessed the market value of the land in questin and also after considering the existing locations,
surroundings, availability of civic amenities and other resources
. The petitioner has also not brought any specific and cogent evidence on record to claim a higher compensation.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.
9.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari),
had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.

The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with LAC no.
67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 11 respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action,
therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
12.

13.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text: 14. I have heard the Ld. Counsel for petitioner and UOI.
None had appeared on behalf of DDA to address the final arguments.
DDA even failed to file written submissions though opportunity was granted.
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to pass judgment on merits of the case.

My issuewise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
16. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ajit Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 18.

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 25 of 200506 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs.
19,45,800/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).

The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same Jai Bhagwan Ors. (2505-06) vs Union Of India (K.S.Nagar, Patti ... on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45909626/
5 compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF LAC no. 67/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 21.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 7/24,
25, 18//1, 10, 19//5/2, 25//1/2, 2/1, 9/2, 10/1 and 4/14 min (001) has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
